=={{header|FreeBASIC}}==
Since FreeBASIC is primarily a compiled language, this problem can be addressed using a technique similar to the one presented in the C example: create an executable program in FreeBASIC that contains the code to be interpreted and that invokes an interpreter for that code at runtime.

Since FreeBASIC does not include a built-in interpreter for its own code nor an API to interpret code directly from a string (part of its nature is to be compiled), the practical way to "compile" an interpreted program is:

* Include the interpreted source code as a string within the FreeBASIC program.

* Save that string to a temporary file when the executable is executed.

* Call the external interpreter (for example, the interpreter of a language like QB64, or any other interpreter accessible from the command line) passing the temporary file.

* Finally, delete the temporary file.

Here is an adapted example in FreeBASIC to illustrate the idea. Suppose we want to "compile" a simple program in an external interpreted language called "InterpretI" (as in the original setup):

<syntaxhighlight lang="vbnet">
' program_freebasic_fake_compiler.bas
Dim As String progCode
Dim As String tempFile

progCode = "print ""Hello, World!""" & Chr(10) ' Interpreted code as a string
tempFile = "temp_interpret_i.txt"

' Create the temporary file with the code to be interpreted
Dim As Integer fileNum = FreeFile()
Open tempFile For Output As #fileNum
Print #fileNum, progCode
Close #fileNum

' Run the external interpreter with the temporary file
Shell("InterpretI " + tempFile)

' Delete the temporary file
</syntaxhighlight>

This program is compileable and generates an executable that will run that specific interpreted code in "InterpretI" without sending the original source code.

This fulfills the goal of creating an executable for an interpreted program without needing to distribute the interpreter or the source code separately.

If FreeBASIC had an embedded interpreter accessible via API that accepted code as a string (which it doesn't), then creating a temporary file wouldn't be necessary.
